💡 Engineering Impact: These features enable architects and DevOps teams to enforce granular security policies like `noexec` on volumes and set specific `emptyDir` permissions, preventing privilege escalation and simplifying compliance without complex workarounds.

title: Kubernetes v1.37: Native PVC Usage Tracking to Cut Cloud Costs
content:
🎯 What Changed: Kubernetes v1.37 promotes the `PersistentVolumeClaimUnusedSinceTime` feature to Beta, natively adding an `Unused` condition to PVCs to track active pod references.
💡 Engineering Impact: This feature empowers storage admins and DevOps to easily identify and automate the cleanup of orphaned PVCs, significantly reducing wasted storage capacity and cloud infrastructure costs without custom scripting.

title: Kubernetes Node Swap GA: Triple Pod Density, Slash Costs
content:
🎯 What Changed: Kubernetes v1.34 officially supports Node Swap, utilizing fast NVMe SSDs to page out dormant memory.
💡 Engineering Impact: This significantly boosts pod density by up to 3x for memory-intensive AI and bursty workloads, optimizing resource utilization and reducing infrastructure costs. It prevents OOM kills and enhances cluster stability, crucial for modern agentic AI.

title: Kubernetes Mandates cgroup v2: Critical Migration for v1.35+ Clusters
content:
🎯 What Changed: Kubernetes has deprecated cgroup v1, with v1.35 defaulting to cgroup v2 and v1.38 slated for its removal, making cgroup v2 the mandatory standard.
💡 Engineering Impact: This shift mandates migration for all Linux nodes to cgroup v2 before upgrading to Kubernetes v1.35+, unlocking superior resource isolation, advanced Memory QoS, and enhanced in-place scaling capabilities. Admins must ensure kernel 5.8+ and compatible container runtimes to prevent kubelet startup failures.
